changes.before: If the descriptor and launch module name both change to study.tools, what prints?
changes.after: Name a Java module and run the main class inside it.

before: module-info.java declares a named module. This tiny module uses only java.base, which is implicitly required. Module names and package names are separate: study.app contains package study. Main.class is a class literal: a Class metadata object for Main. getModule() obtains its module, and getName() reads that module name.

Save the example as study/Main.java, plus module-info.java containing module study.app {}. Compile javac --release 25 -d classes module-info.java study/Main.java. Run java --module-path classes -m study.app/study.Main. Exports would expose a package to other modules; this launcher needs no exports. Changing the descriptor name changes the launch name too.
Expected output or behavior: study.app. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add an exports study directive and explain whom it makes the package accessible to. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A named module groups packages and can state which other modules it needs. module-info.java declares its name. Here, module study.app contains package study; those are separate names. Every named module automatically requires java.base, which provides the basic types used here.

Compile with javac --release 25 -d classes module-info.java study/Main.java. Run java --module-path classes -m study.app/study.Main. The module path locates the module, and -m names its main class. An exports rule would share a package with other modules; this launch needs none.
The program prints study.app. That is the module name declared in module-info.java.
The quiz changes the module name in both its declaration and the launch command. The package name remains study.

before.question: If the descriptor and launch module name both change to study.tools, what prints?
choices: study.app because package study fixes the module name
null because named modules cannot contain main methods
before.explanation: getModule().getName reports the declared named module, independent of the package.

after.question: Change both the declared and launch module name to study.tools. What prints?
choices: study.app, because the package fixes the module name.
null, because named modules cannot contain main methods.
after.explanation: getName reads the declared module name. Changing it to study.tools changes the result, even though the package stays study.
